text: In David Albert's account, what is the 'Past Hypothesis' invoked to explain the thermodynamic arrow of time?
choices: The postulate that the fundamental microscopic laws are themselves time-asymmetric.
The postulate that the macrostate of the universe near its beginning was one of very low entropy.
The assumption that two molecules' velocities are uncorrelated before they collide (molecular chaos).
The claim that the total entropy of any isolated system is exactly conserved over time.
explanation: The Past Hypothesis is Albert's brute posit that the early universe was in an extremely low-entropy macrostate; combined with the Statistical Postulate it grounds entropy increase toward the future. Option 0 is false because the whole puzzle is that the micro-laws are time-symmetric; option 2 names Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz, which the book criticizes for illegitimately smuggling in time asymmetry; option 3 simply denies the Second Law.
